- Primary: Redwood-14B-quant (fp16 + 8-bit quant recommended) — best balance of quality and cost for your multi-turn support use case.
- Fallback: Llama-2-13B (optimized profile) for cost-sensitive paths where we can accept slightly higher latency.

Benchmarks we shared in the call
- Redwood-verified performance profile (p50/p95/p99 latency, token/sec) attached and linked below.
- Customer-specific synthetic runs (TPS at target batch sizes) — we'll run this again on your prompt set.

Action items / next steps
1) Alex / Redwood: run a custom benchmark on the sample prompt set you shared; return results and recommended config (batch size, concurrency, quantization) — target: by Tue EOD PT.
2) Sam: confirm the full prompt set and any safety/formatting constraints (PII redaction, max tokens).
3) Marissa / CS: prep a canary plan and cost estimate for reserved capacity if Finly wants predictable throughput.

Attachments: redwood-verified-profiles-20260328.pdf (performance profile), finly-promptset-sample.json (sample prompts)
Links: https://console.redwood.ai/benchmarks/finly-DEAL-4587

- Redwood-14B-quant @ 80 token response avg: 120 TPS (tokens/sec), 10 req/sec sustained at batch size 8
- Latency (single request, 80 tokens): p50 ~ 65ms, p95 ~ 220ms, p99 ~ 420ms on g5-standard equivalent
- Cost estimate: ~0.8x of our Redwood-34B baseline (depends on quantization profile)

I'll run the custom benchmark tomorrow once you confirm the prompt set. Appreciate the time — excited to help Finly get this into production.

Best,

Hi Sam — quick answers below and details attached. (Forwarding Marissa to coordinate SOC2 & canary.)

1) TPS definition: the 120 TPS number above is tokens/sec aggregated per GPU instance under continuous decode (we quoted tokens/sec in our profile). Practically, with an 80-token average response that converts to ~1.5 requests/sec per instance without batching. With batching (batch size 8) you can get to ~10 req/sec equivalent with lower per-token cost.

2) Latency and batching: the attached Redwood-verified profiles include latency percentiles for both single-request (no batching) and typical batching configurations. For the real-time assistant requirement (p95 < 300ms at 10 concurrent users per shard), here's a recommended config:
- Use dedicated capacity (1 x g5-equivalent per shard)
- Enable small batching (batch size 4–8) with latency SLO guardrails (max_queue_ms=40)
- Quantization: 8-bit + KV cache optimizations — this keeps p95 comfortably <300ms in our tests.

Observed numbers (from the attached profile, g5-equivalent):
- Redwood-14B-quant (no batching): p50 58ms, p95 210ms, p99 380ms
- Redwood-14B-quant (batch size 8): p50 48ms, p95 195ms, p99 350ms
- Llama-2-13B (optimized): p50 72ms, p95 260ms, p99 540ms

3) Compliance: Marissa will follow up with SOC2 package and data residency options (we support region pinning for US/EU).

Next steps I will take this morning:
- Run the custom benchmark on the sample prompt set you uploaded (finly-promptset-sample.json) and share the job link + results (expect by Tue 5pm PT).
- If results look good, we can schedule a 30-minute technical review with your infra/security team and share canary run plan.

Attachments: redwood-verified-profiles-20260328.pdf (contains the tables above and additional TPS curves)
Links: https://console.redwood.ai/benchmarks/finly-DEAL-4587

Thanks — I’ll ping when the benchmark completes.

Best,
Alex
